assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of the active GLP-1 peptide to degradation-resistant agonists, produced a therapeutic class that changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. A clear chain from physiology to medicine with very large, measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of the active peptide), Drucker (receptor biology and gut-pancreas actions) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active form) form a coherent three-person configuration. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen (drug design) is the principal alternative, and the three-name cap forces a real trade-off between physiological discovery and drug development.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, multiple independent large outcome trials and global clinical use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority questions over who first identified the active GLP-1 form
Drug-development contributions may not fit within three names
My account of the history relies on existing knowledge and is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a general method for causal, cell-type-specific control of excitable cells with light, from the discovery of channelrhodopsin function to its use in neurons. A transformative tool across neuroscience with early clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenbock's earlier genetic approach) are distinct steps. Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel is a defensible trio but leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenbock, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of broad independent adoption; the method and its impact are well established. Medical relevance is still emerging, which may matter for a Medicine prize.
uncertainties: Six credited people against a three-laureate limit
Whether a tool-development discovery meets the physiology or medicine criterion as strongly as a disease mechanism

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2, from its link to the t(14;18) lymphoma translocation to the demonstration that it blocks cell death, defined the regulation of apoptosis and enabled BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax). A clear arc from basic cell biology to an approved cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the cloning and characterization of the Bcl-2 family and its role in lymphoma; Vaux showed the pro-survival function of BCL-2 in vivo and its cooperation with Myc. Strasser is a major later contributor. Other groups who identified the translocation and gene are not represented in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed over three decades; clinical approval validates the mechanism. Programmed cell death was recognized earlier through C. elegans genetics, but the BCL-2 family is a distinct contribution.
uncertainties: Which of the four credited names carried the decisive contributions
Contributions of researchers outside the supplied credit cannot be assessed from the longlist

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR, identified as the target of rapamycin, is a central regulator of cell growth and nutrient response with consequences for metabolism, cancer, immunosuppression and ageing biology. Highly original and conceptually unifying.
assessment.attribution: Hall's genetic identification of TOR is the decisive discovery; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and the mammalian target is a natural complement. Sabatini's later work on mTORC1 nutrient sensing is significant, but the supplied credit makes a clean three-way split harder.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed from yeast to mammals; therapeutic exploitation (rapalogs) is real but narrower than the biology. Timely.
uncertainties: Allocation between the TOR genetics and the mammalian target cloning groups is unresolved
Any disputes affecting individual contributors cannot be assessed from the supplied text

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed by the innate immune system, linking infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity. Chen's identification of cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger is a clean mechanistic discovery with strong follow-on.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP) and Barber (STING) are the central contributors. Ishikawa shares the STING discovery, and Wu and Sun were key co-authors in Chen's work. A two-name configuration is coherent, though STING credit overlaps with other groups.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many laboratories and by human genetics of STING-associated disease, but clinical translation is still limited, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of STING agonists and antagonists remains unproven
Priority overlap in the STING discovery between groups

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, with several approved products. A therapeutic landmark combining synthetic receptor design, T-cell engineering and clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulatory CAR design), June (4-1BB CAR and early clinical successes) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) form a plausible trio. Pioneers of the original chimeric receptor concept are not among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation in haematological cancers; benefit in solid tumours is limited and toxicity and cost remain concerns. Recognition is timely, with some risk of being premature for the broader field.
uncertainties: Role of early CAR pioneers outside the credited list
Long-term durability and safety data are still accumulating

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nusinersen showed that antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing can treat a lethal childhood neurodegenerative disease, establishing splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic modality. A strong RNA-processing mechanism with transformative patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing-regulatory mechanism and target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the central, complementary contributors, giving a clean two-name configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long clinical follow-up; now one of several SMA therapies. Maturity is good.
uncertainties: Contributions of the SMN gene discovery and other antisense groups are not credited here
Narrower general scientific scope than the higher-ranked mechanisms

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wnt, from mouse mammary tumour virus integration at Int-1 to a conserved signaling pathway, is a foundational mechanism in development, stem cells and cancer. Highly general and original.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus discovered Int1/Wnt1; the wider pathway was elucidated through Drosophila wingless genetics and many later groups. The two-name configuration captures the discovery but not the pathway components.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed. Varmus's earlier recognition (1989 Nobel Prize, as I recall it) may weigh against a second prize; this is from memory, not verified.
uncertainties: Whether later pathway components deserve recognition ahead of the initial Int1 discovery
Prior Nobel recognition for one credited person
